items.name: Perplexity
items.why: Today’s Nvidia partnership and Portable Computer / local GPU-agent launch create an immediate inference-runtime buying window, and Reo shows High intent with 53 events and 12 active developers in 90 days.
items.message: Aravind — congrats on the Nvidia partnership and the Portable Computer launch. Moving a fully local agent onto user GPUs with a zero-token positioning puts a lot of pressure on compile/runtime performance, memory layout, and consistent latency across heterogeneous devices—areas where cloud-only stacks usually break down. Modular’s MAX inference engine is built for exactly that: high-throughput, portable serving when you need production-grade GPU inference without ballooning cost as surface area expands. If useful, I can share a short briefing on how teams running agentic search/local models tighten time-to-first-token and GPU utilization, and we can map it against your Sonar/frontier routing path. Open to a 20-minute working session this week?

items.name: Gamma
items.why: Today’s Accel-backed Lica acquisition to form an AI design research lab is a fresh new-logo trigger that likely expands generative design inference load.
items.message: Grant — saw Gamma’s acquisition of Accel-backed Lica to build an AI design research lab. That kind of product expansion usually increases multimodal generation volume and R&D iteration rate, which quickly shows up as inference cost and latency pressure—especially if you’re already mixing frontier and open models in production. Modular’s MAX inference engine is built to improve throughput and $/token for generative workloads without forcing a platform rewrite. If useful, I can share how similar design/docs AI teams benchmark MAX against incumbent serving stacks and propose a concrete next step for a side-by-side. Worth 20 minutes this week?

items.name: Liner
items.why: Today’s $36.1M Series C to take evidence-first AI search into enterprise is a clean new-logo funding trigger with light but present Reo engagement.
items.message: Luke — congrats on the $36.1M Series C and the push into enterprise evidence-first AI search. Enterprise search/agents typically drive higher concurrency, longer contexts, and stricter latency SLOs than consumer study use cases—exactly where serving economics and Fireworks-style paths get stressed. Modular’s MAX inference engine helps teams scale model serving with better GPU efficiency and more predictable cost as enterprise traffic ramps. If you’re planning infra for that expansion, I’d be glad to walk through a short MAX evaluation against your current mix. Open to a brief call this week?

items.name: Abridge
items.why: This week’s rollout of context-aware clinical intelligence to every clinician at partner health systems implies a step-change in real-time inference volume, with Moderate Reo engagement supporting outreach.
items.message: Shiv — Abridge making context-aware clinical intelligence available to every clinician at partner health systems is a meaningful production scale-up beyond ambient documentation. Hospital-wide copilots are latency-sensitive and multi-tenant, so inference cost and reliability tend to become first-order constraints quickly—especially at note volumes already in the millions per week. Modular’s MAX inference engine helps clinical AI teams raise throughput and tighten serving economics without sacrificing responsiveness. Given some recent Modular engagement from Abridge developers, this seems like a good week to compare MAX against your current Baseten-oriented path. Open to a brief technical call this week?
